articleName: The Promise of Tutoring for PreK–12 Learning: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Experimental Evidence
articleDescription: Nickow, Oreopoulos and Quan (2024) present the journal version of their systematic review and meta-analysis of tutoring field experiments. The American Educational Research Journal article reports a pooled effect of 0.288 standard deviations (SE 0.029) and examines variation by tutor type, grade, frequency and setting.
claimName: The 2024 tutoring meta-analysis estimated a pooled learning gain of 0.288 standard deviations.
claimDescription: Nickow, Oreopoulos and Quan (2024) report an overall pooled effect size of 0.288 standard deviations (SE 0.029, p < .001) across tutoring field experiments. Effects tend to be largest with teachers or paraprofessionals, earlier grades, at least three days per week and during school; the pooled estimate does not describe every implementation.
locator: American Educational Research Journal 61(1), abstract, pp. 74–107
